exposure: semi-automated SSI surveillance using the indicators 'antibiotic prescription', 'microbiological data' and 'administrative data'
cohort: Women who underwent breast surgeries in 2018 and caesarean sections between May 2013 and December 2019 at a tertiary care hospital in Germany
finding: Semi-automated surveillance systems for surgical site infections (SSIs) may reduce workload by maintaining high sensitivity, but the effectiveness depends on the type of surgery, local circumstances, and thorough digitalization.
mod_finding: For caesarean sections, semi-automated surveillance using a combination of indicators had a sensitivity of 94.4% for detecting SSIs.
